<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via expireAfter (literal, a string literal in settings), maxAge (literal, a string literal in settings))_
- `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`  _(via maxAge (literal, a string literal in settings))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via settingsCommon (symbol, a field of const object ar; a field of const object fr; a field of const object ptBR; a field of const object zhHant))_
- `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`  _(via settingsCommon (symbol, a field of const object ar; a field of const object fr; a field of const object ptBR; a field of const object zhHant))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via expireAfter (literal, a string literal in settings))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/api/v1 (route, 118 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d8b22954ad3040fe8ff1cb30667101847b694584` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5630807a76f7664beb861dca7d9734aa3d8f5d17` — the merge of head `dd6a80232001d7c0bb9dbc49dfbc3d87d76b7b08` into base `d8b22954ad3040fe8ff1cb30667101847b694584`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5630807a76f7664beb861dca7d9734aa3d8f5d17 && git checkout 5630807a76f7664beb861dca7d9734aa3d8f5d17
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d8b22954ad3040fe8ff1cb30667101847b694584 dd6a80232001d7c0bb9dbc49dfbc3d87d76b7b08 && git checkout -B drift-repro d8b22954ad3040fe8ff1cb30667101847b694584 && git merge --no-ff dd6a80232001d7c0bb9dbc49dfbc3d87d76b7b08

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d8b22954ad3040fe8ff1cb30667101847b694584
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d8b22954ad3040fe8ff1cb30667101847b694584` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · 2026-11-06T11:32Z · #30512 (package 6 of 11, service-settings, first half)

Head-sha: dd6a80232001d7c0bb9dbc49dfbc3d87d76b7b08 (a relay update-branch merge of `main` over the reviewed `9c22c667` / `9e0f2cd6`, bringing in #30908, the fix for the #30873 Test Core 6/8 timeout that turned the earlier heads red; the diff against `main` is the same 7 files, +2694/−3)

- **Shape:** 7 files, +2694/−3. Inside claim 6672078792; not governed; one commit on `origin/main` `a2f523aa`.
  - Four new locale files: zh-Hant, ar, fr and pt-BR.
  - `translations/index.ts` registers them in `settingsBuiltinTranslations`.
  - The coverage test holds the four locales to full coverage.
  - One patch changeset.
- **Seat ruling (a) applied:** the handover `70f9870a` is carried without the `localization-currency-lock` and `localization-locale-options` hunks and their test hunk, because #30734 owns those tables. The zh-Hant brand names are in Traditional script.
- **Spot check (read in the diff):**
  - No new public export. The package entry still re-exports `settingsBuiltinTranslations` plus the en, zh-CN and ja-JP named bundles. The map gains four locale keys, which is data, not shape.
  - zh-Hant reads as Traditional, for example 寄件者名稱 and 預設簡訊範本.
  - `${content}` in the SMS template help is kept literally in single-quoted strings, the same way zh-CN and es-ES carry it.
  - No added string starts with the article `os `, and the dev also ran `check-cli-command-ids`.
  - No assertion is relaxed.
- **Gates:** every check-run on this head has concluded: 48 distinct checks, the latest run of each 35 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure (Test Core 6/8 green with #30908 in). Locally (dev report 6679996540):
  - Tree build 118/118, service-settings 71 files / 1313 tests, typecheck VERDICT 0.
  - The full `check-i18n-bundles` (10 packages), stale-fill and `check-cli-command-ids` exit 0.
  - The 60 derived families, `pnpm lint` and the docs & code guards lane (56) exit 0 at `f8d192f9`, the same patch id.
  - The first bundle check at this head refused platform-objects' `requiresFeature` group (#30810) only on a stale spec build. It passed after the rebuild, so the refusal is not this PR's.
- **Contract:** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, confirmed from the diff.
- **Landing:** ready, then auto-merge, through the relay. Settings B (ru, de, ko) follows on the same branch.
